questions.q: What is the main thing a portfolio proves that a résumé alone does not?
options: That you own many software licenses
Judgment: framing a question, working through messy data, and reaching a recommendation
That you can list many tools
That you have memorized SOQL syntax
questions.explain: Hiring managers use portfolios to watch your reasoning from question to recommendation, which a list of tools cannot show.

questions.q: Which set best matches the recommended one-page project structure?
options: Logo, tagline, price, testimonials
Question, data, method, findings, recommendation, limitations
Only screenshots of dashboards
Only the SOQL queries with no explanation
questions.explain: The structure makes every project skimmable and covers judgment, method, evidence, and honesty about limits.

questions.q: Why is it useful to state limitations in a portfolio project?
options: It builds trust by showing honesty about sample size and assumptions
It lowers your chances of being interviewed
It replaces the need for findings
It is required by Salesforce
questions.explain: Naming limits shows analytical maturity and honesty, which hiring managers value.

questions.q: You want to show a project based on your current employer's real sales data. What is the recommended approach?
options: Post screenshots with customer names blurred lightly
Publish everything on Tableau Public
Do not publish it; use your own Developer Edition data or a fully anonymized description instead
Email the raw data to recruiters
questions.explain: Real employer data should never be published. Use self-generated data in a Developer Edition org or describe the work in generalized, anonymized terms.

questions.q: How many portfolio projects does the lesson suggest aiming for?
options: As many as possible, even if unfinished
Exactly one, with no write-up
Two or three polished projects
Ten quick screenshots
questions.explain: Two or three polished, well-explained projects beat many half-finished ones.
